title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: Recomputing a Disputed Demurrage Line
content:
## Clause

Demurrage and Detention Free Time demurrage that is challenged for misapplied rates or misapplied free time is priced afresh by the desk, using only the movement dates on file for the record and the product the record carries, as follows.

**Separate clocks.** Import demurrage is timed between discharge and the full gate-out and measured against the product's import demurrage free days; export demurrage is timed between the full gate-in and loading and measured against its export demurrage free days. The calendar days between the two dates are the days used; whatever exceeds the free days is chargeable, and the first of those chargeable days is position 1 of the slab count.

**Merged clock.** One clock covers the whole import stay from discharge until the empty is back, or the whole export stay from empty pickup until loading, and the merged free days are set against it. Among its chargeable days, an import record treats as demurrage those dated no later than the full gate-out, and an export record those dated after the full gate-in. Import demurrage takes position 1 at the merged clock's first chargeable day; export demurrage takes up the count where the detention line booked on the record leaves off, following on from the chargeable days entered on that line.

**Slabs.** A day sits in slab 1 while its position in the count is within the first slab length, in slab 2 while within the first two lengths added together, in slab 3 while within all three lengths added together, and in slab 4 once past them.

**Pricing.** Every repriced day is charged the demurrage rate of its slab within the rate class that applies, adjusted for any uplift the booking's cargo type brings. The recomputed amount is the sum of those day charges, rounded once to the cent.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A merged-clock export record whose detention line shows 6 chargeable days has 5 demurrage days to reprice. With slab lengths of 4, 4 and 8, those days occupy positions 7 to 11: two in slab 2 and three in slab 3. At repricing rates of 100.00 in slab 2 and 150.00 in slab 3, with no uplift, the recomputed amount is 650.00. If the line had been invoiced at 700.00, the overcharge found would be 50.00.
